title: Nine Letters of Breaking
subtitle: 代码与密码 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 代码与密码（科学与技术·信息与编码）
meta: 主题语境：代码与密码（科学与技术·信息与编码）　|　核心词汇：code　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 code 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 my mother was sent to break ① code she could not read, and she said the breaking was the whole of the lesson. The ② code, meaning the cipher and not the law, was nine letters long and was broken by whoever came last; code, she said, is the only thing in a message that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ code in that message had the same key, and the ④ code at the end, meaning the one the officer kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever broke properly. Code, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ code was the whole of the trade, meaning the rule it carried and not the cipher. The ⑥ code, meaning the rule and not any of that, is the only thing in a trade that everybody keeps and nobody questions; code, he said, is either something you break or the only word that means both a cipher and a rule. She said the rule is the part they remember.

By 1980 the ⑦ code had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the key. The ⑧ code of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine letters and eleven years of breaking; code, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ code I remember is the one at the end, which was broken in 1985 and is still described as the hardest in the county. A ⑩ code, my grandmother said in 1990, is the only thing that improves by being broken; every code, she said, is a rule that has agreed to look like a cipher. She said the rule was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 密码（指那组密文本身，与那条法令相对）
C. 固定搭配：break a code 破译一组密码
D. n. 密码（指那条讯息里每一组）
E. n. 密码（指末尾那一组）
F. n. 准则（抽象：它承载的那条规矩）
G. n. 那条规矩（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The code, meaning the cipher and not the law
code was the whole of the trade
the code had become a number in a report
The code of the whole thing
A code, my grandmother said in 1990

answers.why: break a code 意为“破译一组密码”，1965 年母亲被派去破译她读不懂的那组密码。
code 意为“密码、代码”，指那组密文本身而不是那条法令，共九个字母，由最后来的人破译。
code 指那条讯息里每一组密码，每一组都是同样的密钥。
code 指末尾那一组（军官保留的那一组），是唯一有人认真破译过的。
code 意为“准则”，抽象指它承载的那条规矩，父亲说 code 就是那门行业的全部。
code 为抽象用法，指那条规矩本身，是一门行业里人人都守、却没人质疑的东西。
code 意为“密码、代码”，到 1980 年这组 code 成了报告里的一个数字。
code 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个字母和十一年的破译。
code 意为“密码”，我记得的是末尾那一组，1985 年破译，至今仍被说成全县最难的。
code 为抽象总称，祖母说一组密码是唯一会因为被认真破译而变好的东西。
